methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series E → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.4x) to $15.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $2.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Divergent
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series E), post-money $2.3B

data.narrative:
Fairmat, a Series E robotics and manufacturing company that has raised approximately €95M ($103M) to date, is evaluated against a comparables universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company (277810.KQ). The peer set includes Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity, all operating in the same sector at comparable or adjacent funding stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method, using a $15.0B total-raised proxy as the base and applying a 1.4x Series E step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $21.0B. The Peer-Median method across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Divergent (Series E, $2.3B), Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), and Locus Robotics (Series F, $2.0B)—yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range of $2.0B to $2.3B.

The material divergence between these methods reflects uncertainty in appropriate base assumptions. The stage-progression approach relies on a total-raised proxy not independently validated here; the peer-median anchors to observable transactions but a three-company sample carries limited statistical power. The triangulated range spans $1.7B (low) to $24.1B (high), with a median of $11.5B. Key uncertainties include revenue, margin profile, and growth trajectory relative to peers—data not provided in this analysis.
